item.description: 5 Points Gallery, an artist-owned contemporary art gallery in downtown Durham, is pleased to announce an exhibition of paintings by Featured Artist King Nobuyoshi Godwin, whose vibrant, imaginative work reflects his experience of autism and synesthesia. Bringing together expressive animals, vivid colors, and numbers that convey emotion, Godwin creates playful worlds filled with unexpected connections. Several of you have suggested this as a ride, and I'm pretty sure a few of you have ridden it with some group or other, so I'd welcome any suggestions, including where to get off of the Neuse River Trail to head over to the brewery. item.title: Sperling Center Presents Undergraduate Doc Fest — Mon Nov 30, 7:00 PM — Rubenstein Arts Center
item.description:
The Sperling Center for Jewish Studies at Duke University is pleased to present its Undergraduate Documentary Film Festival, featuring original documentary films created by Duke undergraduates exploring Jewish history, culture, religion, memory, and contemporary Jewish life.
Drawing on archival research, oral histories, interviews, and personal narratives, student filmmakers bring Jewish Studies scholarship to life through the medium of film. This year's projects explore the history and contemporary experiences of Morocco's Sephardic Jewish community and the complex dynamics of Jewish-Muslim relations, as well as the story of the family of Keith Siegel, who was taken hostage during the October 7 attacks. Through these films, students examine questions of identity, memory, resilience, intercommunal relations, and the ways global events resonate within local communities, including at Duke and in Durham.

item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. item.description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.
Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art.
